turns.prompt_text: A friend gave me some zucchini from this garden I don't know what to do with it Attached 1 file. - ccf70d54-0b4d-4430-8dc1-c6884a5dd2e0
turns.response_html:
That giant one top-side is a classic garden "overgrow"—it went from small to absolute monster overnight!

Because of the massive size difference between the two, you'll actually want to treat them a bit differently in the kitchen to get the best results.

1. The Small Zucchini (Standard Use)

The smaller one has thin skin, low water content, and small tender seeds. It’s perfect for fast, high-heat cooking where you want texture.

  • Sauté or Pan-Fry: Slice into thick coins or half-moons, toss with olive oil, salt, pepper, and garlic, and sear over medium-high heat until golden brown.
  • Pasta Toss: Dice it small and toss directly into a warm pasta dish, letting the residual heat cook it through while keeping a bit of crunch.
  • Grilled Skewers: Slice thick, brush with oil, and grill directly until charred.

2. The Big Zucchini (Preparation & Baking)

Large garden zucchinis tend to have tough skin, large spongy seed centers, and a lot of water. Don't worry, though—they are fantastic for baking and stuffing!

Prep Tip for Giant Zucchini: Slice it in half lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out the seedy, pithy center. You can also peel the skin if it feels particularly tough.

  • Zucchini Bread or Muffins: Shred the firm outer flesh using a box grater. Squeeze out excess moisture with a paper towel or dish towel, then fold it into quick bread or sweet muffin batter.
  • Stuffed Zucchini Boats: Scoop out the center to create a trough. Fill it with seasoned ground meat, marinara, breadcrumbs, and cheese, then bake at 375°F (190°C) until tender.
  • Fritters: Shred the flesh, mix with an egg, a bit of flour, parmesan, and herbs, then pan-fry spoonfuls until crisp.

Storage Tip

If you aren't ready to use them right away, keep them uncut and dry in the crisper drawer of your fridge. They'll easily hold up for a week. If you shred the large one for baking, you can freeze the shredded zucchini in sealed freezer bags for later use!
